notes.title: Unity controversy + Future of Crumple Zone
notes.notes:
Hey folks, how's life?

As many of you probably know, Crumple Zone has been built on the Unity Engine.
There is quite some controversy and outrage going on related to that at the moment, with a lot of misinformation and overreaction, so I wanted to share my thoughts and what it means for the future of Crumple Zone.

First of all, this controversial "install fee" only comes into effect after a certain number of installs, which is way beyond what most indie titles, including Crumple Zone, will reach. So in that regard it is actually not that much different from other business models like, let's say Unreal/Epic, where there's a revenue share percentage only after reaching a certain volume of sales - so the Unity model is likely actually still "cheaper" at the end of the day, from a developers perspective, if you're selling high numbers.

In other words, from all the info I know, I don't expect this to affect the distribution or pricing policy of Crumple Zone in any way. On the contrary, I plan to engage in more ways to offer more discounted sales in the upcoming months, both on Steam but also on other platforms, so keep an eye out for future deals.

[b]HOWEVER, that being said, the latest events with Unity are the last straw in a long history of questionable decisions, business strategies and PR statements that are completely against my own believes and ideologies when it comes to creating games, which is why I will stop any further game development based on the Unity Engine.[/b]

To give a bit more of context, back in late 2017 when I started developing Crumple Zone, I had the feeling that Unity was more of an underdog and interesting alternative to a mega-corp product like Unreal, and also was intrigued by the challenge to build a proper PC game with Unity vs. all the mobile stuff that this engine is mostly known for.
Another strong reason was the availability of well done existing third party libraries for driving physics, something I could not find elsewhere.
But in a kind of ironic turn of events, it seems Epic nowadays is much more caring about small developers and giving powerful tools into the hands of everyone, with no monetization hurdles (note: you still have to pay for a Unity license), while Unity is really showing the face of a greedy megacorp.

Ok so what does that mean for future development of Crumple Zone?

1) I was pondering the idea to do an upgraded / enhanced version of the base CZ game for a while, that would include more content, better visuals, and potentially stuff like online MP and VR support, and already started implementing some of it. Kind of like Crumple Zone 1.5 or "Ultimate Edition", if you will. But now I will scrap those plans and go straight for a proper sequel in a new engine.

2) Despite that, please don't think Crumple Zone is an "abandoned game", I will still fully support it, just don't expect any major updates.

3) Work on Crumple Zone 2 has started and it will be build on Unreal Engine 5. Yes, there you have it.

4) Switching to Unreal will have both positive and negative consequences:
[list]
[*] 	I will not be able to use any of the code from CZ1 and need to rebuild most of the gameplay systems from scratch again
[*] 	This, and just learning the engine in general (already made some good progress but still a long way) will take time
[/list]
	BUT these downsides will be out-weighted by the benefits:
[list]
[*] 	Whereas CZ1, intentionally, has a simplistic charm when it comes to graphics as a homage to PS1 days, this time round I will go all in and aim for stunning AA visuals
[*] 	I will incorporate Online MP from the very start to integrate it well vs. trying to do it after the fact like in CZ1 where it proved to be very challenging
[*] 	I already started implementing the driving physics completely myself this time, not using a library, so I have full control of the way the physics handle and feel
[*] 	The cool assets and systems that Unreal offers out of the box for creating big levels even as a small studio / single person will allow for a bigger scope in general
[/list]

On top of that, Crumple Zone 2 will also see a shift in terms of gameplay and setting - don't worry, it will still be an arcade crash racer with constant over the top action and tie into the lore already created in the first game.
I cannot go into details yet, but I will share a first glimpse at the current prototype with you soon, that may give you some food for speculation.

Bottom line: I will be honest about it: due to everything mentioned it will take a while until CZ2 releases, but I assure you, my humble goal is to make it nothing less than the best most exciting arcade crash racer possible, taking in all the experience and feedback I gained from CZ1, combined with the exciting new possibilities thanks to Unreal Engine 5.

Sorry for the lengthy read, but as always, I try to be as transparent as possible about what's going on behind the scenes.

Would love to hear your thoughts about the situation in the comments below!

Keep on (crash) racing
OutOfTune / Moritz

notes.title: Easter Special Discount + the state of things
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, I hope you are doing well!

Crumple Zone is on sale with a great discount this Easter, so if you are still undecided or you know someone who is, now is the perfect time to pick it up.

As far as development goes, I was able to update the game's engine which clears the way to work on online multiplayer and VR support. I actually started working on both but there is a lot of work still left to get it to a releasable state. Plus, in these times I have to take extra care for my family and find less time to work on the game. So I can't promise any ETA yet, but it's coming!

Stay tuned and - most importantly - stay healthy

notes.title: Halloween Update including paintjob mod support (beta)!
notes.notes:
In today's spooky update you'll find two new Halloween-themed paintjob graphics.
But that's not the interesting part - they are actually show casing a new game feature: paintjob modding!

It's in "beta" state for now because of two reasons:
1) I haven't tested it thoroughly yet, so please let me know of any bugs you might find.
2) I haven't integrated it with the steamworks system yet, that's the next step, so you can easily share these paintjobs. For now you can start modding on your own at least.

I will post a more detailed guide in the community section soon but here is the quick version:

Put a PNG image with square dimensions into one of the folders in:

[i]<Crumple Zone installation directory>/Mods/Paintjobs/<Car Name>[/i]

All paintjobs can be selected for all cars but I added a compability hint that suggests which car it works best on. I will explain why that's the case later, too.

By the way can view the Halloween paintjobs as examples and there are also templates available in the paintjobs folder.

Credits for the Halloween graphics goes to:
"PhotoComix Mandala" on flickr
"stux" on pixabay

Have fun, give modding a shot, post screenshots and stay tuned for more info in the near future! ːInfectedHeadː

notes.title: Photo Mode + Opponent Driver Profiles
notes.notes:
This updates includes two new features that were requested most in the recent survey:


[b]Opponent Driver Profiles / Back Stories[/b]

Ramming into opponents is a lot more fun when you know who you are actually dealing with!
Now you can find out more about each character in the
[b]Extras -> Opponent Profiles[/b]
menu.
Note: Any resemblances to real or fictional characters are purely coincidental! That being said, can you figure out all the "coincidences"? ;-)


[b]Photo Mode[/b]

Now you can capture all those insane moments in Crumple Zone in all their glory! Simply open photo mode from the pause menu. If you want to take/share a screenshot, there are two ways to go about it:

1) Use Steam or another capture software (e.g. Fraps)

Press "H" to hide the Photo Mode UI and then trigger your capture. For Steam, the Steam in-game overlay has to be enabled. The default key on Steam is F12.

2) Use Crumple Zone's capture feature

You can press A/Enter to trigger a screenshot capture within Crumple Zone. The UI will be hidden automatically. All screenshots are lossless PNG and saved here:
<Your main Steam folder>\steamapps\common\Crumple Zone\CrumpleZone_Data


There are also a couple of smaller fixes/improvements in this update:
- support for 16:10 resolutions (cutscene texts are no longer cut off)
- improved camera manual spin control when reversing (no longer inverted)
- player 2 in split screen no longer has a blank avatar
- fixed a bug where sound controls in pause menu would stay on screen when exiting pause menu

notes.title: Survey results + future plans + other news
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Hope you're doing well. I'm back from summer vacation and now it's the perfect time to enlighten you about some of the news and plans for Crumple Zone.

Ok first off and better late than never - Crumple Zone now has a Twitter account @CrumpleZoneGame
The steam store page and community hub will still be the main focus for major updates but Twitter might be a cool place for everything else such as gameplay videos, off topic stuff etc. Also, if you like Crumple Zone and retweet the occasional post, it could help spread the word about the game.


[b]Survey results[/b]

Anyways, now to the probably more interesting topic: The survey about the future of Crumple Zone is closed - thanks to anyone who took part!
I'll show the most important results and tell you what it means for the game's road map.

[i]Major new feature[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34868665/ded5342aee98d05e167addc786960088bc8e09ac.jpg[/img]

This one surprised me the most. I could have bet that online multiplayer wins but it actually came in last. Ok, it needs to be considered that there are probably some players who haven't bought the game because it lacks online MP and they did not participate in the survey. So I still think it's important but I find modding support very interesting too, so I will start with that.
More on that in the road map.

[i]Minor new feature[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34868665/8c25d9bfc8cde6e679adc75f35437cf6b914e9fb.jpg[/img]

Pretty close, but two features stand out, Photo Mode and Opponent Back Stories / Profiles.

[i]Content[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34868665/a67dbfedda6bc86a0b66cdb1459d55605f65a70d.jpg[/img]
"Tracks" were leading here for quite some time but were overtaken by "Cars". Still quite close though, so I will try to add both in the future.

[i]Platforms[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34868665/ed7389a3dfde4b02be3b2c2f78b3a1a639751fc1.jpg[/img]

This is quite interesting, Android is the clear winner, but Virtual Reality, although being a niche sort of thing, came in second. That's cool, I got a VR headset myself and enjoy the technology, so I might try something out. With both Android and VR though, it's more of an experimental thing - if I find the time, I'll check out how much effort is needed to port to those platforms and whether it's feasible at all, while updates for the regular PC version always have priority.


[b]Development Roadmap[/b]

With the insights gathered from the survey results, I plan the following updates for Crumple Zone:
[i]1. Minor update in September[/i]
I want to release an update this month which includes the 2 top "minor" features from the poll, a photo mode and opponent profiles + some smaller fixes and improvements
[i]2. Workshop integration with custom paintjobs[/i]
After the minor update is done, I'll look into integrating the steam workshop API and as a sort of proof of concept, I will use it to allow you to upload and add custom paintjob graphics to the game. This will be a very simple use case that is perfect for getting the workshop system to run before adding more complex modding capabilities.
[i]3. Track and/or car modding support[/i]
Once the workshop integration stands, I'll work on a way to integrate custom tracks or cars. This will be some time at the end of this year probably. Although cars got more votes, I might start with tracks because they are less complex and specific to the game, so they should be easier to do. I could even imagine an in-game track editor.
[i]4. Other platforms and online multiplayer[/i]
I will start working on these but not before next year

I hope this gives you a rough idea about what to expect in the future, I will go into more detail when the time is right, so stay tuned and happy crumpling!

notes.title: Community members in credits section + screen resolution fix
notes.notes:
With the latest (small) update I added a special section in the credits to honor all of those Crumple Zone players who helped greatly in improving and shaping the game.
You probably know who you are if you're reading this, but have a look to make sure! :)
By the way, if you like to have a different name or maybe even your real name listed there, just let me know.

Of course, this section will be updated in the future and anyone who stands out in the community as very helpful and supportive of the game will join the hall of fame in the credits! You guys are great and I don't want to leave that unmentioned.

There is another small improvement in this update concerning screen resolutions, well more precicely "uncommon" screen resolution that aren't part of the basic set of supported resolutions.
Basically what it does is add the native desktop resolution in case it is not part of the default resolutions.
I haven't tested this extensively so I hope it works as expected and fixes some cases of players reporting they can't play with their native resolution on laptops (1366x768).
Screen ratios other than 16:9 aren't officially supported yet but I will try to make the UI responsive at some point so nothing weird happens in other aspect ratios.

There are more announcements coming at the end of the month, so stay tuned and happy car smashing! >:)

notes.title: New patch including handbrake for all you show-offs out there!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34868665/4a5d07736bbffbdd0d6d0b7db6ec571b123e19b6.gif[/img]

Your wish is my command, and a couple of you requested a handbrake feature, so here it is!
Just tap it to provoke oversteering and get quicker around tight corners.
In arenas, you can use it to make quick 180s at slower speeds.

Use the "B" button on Xbox Controllers, right Control on Keyboard... or equivalent (?) on other controllers (too much to list).

There are also a couple of more "moving objects" added to some levels. I will not spoil anything, try to spot them on your own. I can only say... Yvan eht nioj! (No I'm not having a stroke)

notes.title: Get ready to Crumple!
notes.notes:
[b]Crumpe Zone has just been released![/b]

For a very reasonable price, you can re-live the golden era of over-the-top senseless car smashing.

Please keep in mind that this is only the beginning. Don't worry, I promise you get a complete coherent experience when you buy the game today. But there's much more that can be added and improved if you support the game and it's development in the future.

So if you like the game, connect with other players and the devs in the community hub and spread the word about Crumple Zone in streams, chats etc.

Let's make demolition derby games great again!
